record.what_it_does: Private-market company, deal, investor and fund data platform with a paid Direct Data API.
record.auth_notes: Static API key sent as "Authorization: PB-Token {key}" (header format from third-party guides, not confirmed on PitchBook docs). There is no OAuth for the REST API. The key belongs to the customer organization, so it isn't a per-end-user flow. The Premium MCP connector uses a sign-in (likely OAuth), but that is not a general developer API.
record.access_notes: API keys come from a paid API add-on, provisioned through the PitchBook account manager or org administrator. There is no self-serve key and no free tier. It needs an existing PitchBook subscription plus a Direct Data contract. A sandbox key also has to be requested.
record.api_breadth_notes: Base URL https://api.pitchbook.com. It covers companies, deals, investors, funds and similar entities. The docs sit behind the platform login, so the operation count could not be checked.
record.mcp_notes: https://premium.mcp.pitchbook.com/mcp, the "PitchBook Premium" connector. Claude's marketplace lists it as made by PitchBook, and PitchBook's help page calls it the Premium Connector. It requires sign-in and is for PitchBook clients. Strac, Apify, Merge and Vinkius also offer third-party wrappers.
record.blocker_notes: The API is a paid, contract-gated add-on with no self-serve credentials, and the docs are behind login. Composio cannot get keys alone. Each customer would need their own API contract, or the work would go through a PitchBook partnership. The official remote MCP is a possible alternative path for users who are PitchBook clients.

evidence.quote: PitchBook API keys are provisioned as part of a paid API add-on rather than generated self-serve.
PitchBook authenticates API requests with a static API key
PitchBook also offers a test sandbox environment that uses the same base URL with a separate key.

record.needs_human: PitchBook's own help pages (pitchbook.com/help/pitchbook-api and the Premium Connector page) returned 403 to me. The auth, access and sandbox findings therefore come from a third-party integrator (Frontegg) and search summaries. A human should check them on PitchBook's pages or with a PitchBook rep. Open points: the exact auth header, whether an OpenAPI spec or webhooks exist, API breadth, and the MCP connector's auth type and licensing terms.
